help.tips[0].examples[0].en: She learnt new words every day and bought many books.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Regular verbs add -te to the stem: kauf-te. ich takes no extra ending, and -ete is only for stems ending in t, d or consonant + m/n.
help.tips[0].en.text: lernen → lern-te: lernte, lerntest, lernte, lernten, lerntet, lernten. kaufen → kaufte. spielen → spielte. hören → hörte. machen → machte.
help.tips[0].en.title: Stem + -te + ending
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: He waited an hour, then he opened the door.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: It rained all day, and we talked about old times.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The stem wart- ends in -t, so it needs the extra -e-: wart-e-te, and wir adds -n: warteten.
help.tips[1].en.text: arbeiten → arbeitete · warten → wartete · reden → redete · öffnen → öffnete · atmen → atmete · regnen → regnete. The same -e- you know from er arbeitet.
help.tips[1].en.title: -ete after t, d, and consonant + m/n
help.tips[1].en.trap: 'he worked' looks like it should be 'er arbeitet' + something; but arbeitet is the present. The past is arbeitete: three e's in a row, and it is right.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Yesterday I worked late. — Back then he worked in Berlin.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: From 2015 to 2019 I worked as a waiter in Vienna.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: In everyday speech Germans use the Perfekt for most verbs; spielte belongs in written stories and reports.
help.tips[2].en.text: Write: stories, reports, CVs (Von 2015 bis 2019 arbeitete ich …), fairy tales. Speak: Perfekt (Ich habe gearbeitet) — except war, hatte, konnte, musste, wollte, which are Präteritum even in speech.
help.tips[2].en.title: When to write it, when to say it
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: I lived – he lived – we lived
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: I made – he made – you (pl.) made
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The er/sie form equals the ich form in the Präteritum: wohnte, with no -t. wohntet is for ihr, wohnten for wir/sie.
help.tips[3].en.text: In the Präteritum the first and third person always match: ich machte / er machte, ich sagte / er sagte. If you write 'er machtet', you've added a present-tense -t that doesn't belong.
help.tips[3].en.title: ich = er, and no -t
help.context.en: Back then I lived in a small village. I worked in the bakery and learnt English in the evenings. Every Sunday I played football with my friends, and afterwards we talked for hours in the café. That time lasted only two years, but I laughed more then than ever before.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: No -t in the third person Präteritum.
help.hookEn: Write about your past the way German stories are written — one simple -te pattern turns kaufen into kaufte and wohnen into wohnte.
help.introEn: You already recognise the Präteritum; now you write in it. Regular (weak) verbs form it by adding -te to the stem and then the past endings: ich arbeitete, du arbeitetest, er arbeitete, wir arbeiteten, ihr arbeitetet, sie arbeiteten. Stems ending in -t, -d, or a consonant cluster with -m/-n (arbeiten, reden, warten, öffnen, atmen) insert an -e- before the -te so it can be pronounced: arbeitete, redete, öffnete. The first and third person singular are identical (ich lernte / er lernte), and there is no -t in the third person. This is the tense of stories, reports, newspapers and any written account of what happened; in speech, the Perfekt is still normal — except for war, hatte and the modals, which are always Präteritum.
help.rememberEn[1]: ich = er; -n for wir/sie; no -t anywhere in the third person.
help.recallEn.known: From "Präteritum: erste Schritte": stem + -te, and ich = er.
help.recallEn.today: The -ete verbs, and when to write the Präteritum and when to say the Perfekt.
sentences[0].whyEn: Regular: stem + -ete on a t-stem — arbeitete.
sentences[3].whyEn: ich: -te with no further ending — schickte.
sentences[7].whyEn: fragte — regular; and fragen nach + dative.
sentences[11].whyEn: the -fn stem needs the e: öffnete.
sentences[13].whyEn: d-stem plus helper e, plural: redeten.
sentences[15].whyEn: d-stem: badeten — with the helper e.
sentences[16].whyEn: the -gn stem: regnete — the e makes it sayable.
sentences[17].whyEn: ihr takes -tet; on the t-stem that gives wartetet — three t's!
